stem:
Kiara's science club sets up a pinhole projector in the school yard to watch a solar eclipse on a white card. A classmate wants to look at the Sun through ordinary sunglasses instead, and another wants to glance when only a thin crescent remains.

Which claims about safety are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Watching the Sun's projected image on the white card with the pinhole projector can be a safe method.
Looking at the Sun through ordinary sunglasses is a safe substitute for proper eclipse protection.
It is unsafe to look directly at the Sun during the eclipse without proper protection.
When only a thin crescent of the Sun remains, it is safe to look directly without protection.

teacher.key_rationale: A pinhole projection onto a card can be safe; ordinary sunglasses and unprotected viewing of a thin crescent are not safe.
